course_description:
Discipline-specific inquiry into intervention/treatment efficacy and effectiveness within Health Sciences Research.

Research is an essential component of clinical practice in the health and rehabilitation sciences. This course presents an extension to the “Consumer” and “Generator” dimensions of the HRSS “Consumer-Collaborator-Generator” Research Development model.

The course provides specific knowledge and/or skills in research principles and methods to enable clinicians-in-training to:

This is an interdisciplinary course involving students from Physiotherapy, Occupational Therapy, and Speech Pathology . Therefore, learning activities are presented with an interdisciplinary focus.

The course builds on the HRSS Stage 2 Health Sciences Research Discovery I Course [HRSS3101], which has provided students with competencies for building knowledge and improving clinical practice using common Health Sciences Research methods.

The course precedes the HRSS Stage 4 Investigation Projects, which involve either a group-based service quality improvement project (HRSS4201), or an individual Health Sciences Research Advanced Project (HRSS4300).

Additional timetable information
A detailed timetable is provided on the HRSS3102 Blackboard Site under "Course Information".
Online Lectures via Zoom
Six 1-hour online lectures are delivered across different weeks. Four lectures take place in
Week 1
to introduce the course and assessment tasks and to support learning in evaluating quantitative literature. One lecture in
Week 6
focuses on synthesising findings from quantitative research, and an additional lecture in
Week 10
addresses the evaluation of qualitative literature.
An optional 1-hour online lecture is delivered in
Week 2
on statistics revision.
All online lectures will be recorded and made available on Blackboard.
Tutorials (in-person on campus)
The discipline-specific tutorials (2 hours each) are delivered in person during
Weeks 3, 5, 7, 9, 11, and 12
. The sessions are run like a journal club, where students review practice-related papers using CASP checklists. The sessions include hands-on activities to help apply what was taught and better understand research quality and usefulness. The sessions also support assignment development through feedback and clarification of expectations. In-person quizzes are conducted during these tutorials.
Drop-in Sessions via Zoom (optional)
An optional 1-hour drop-in session are delivered at
5:00pm on Tuesdays in Weeks 4, 8, and 12.
These sessions aim to address module-related questions and provide support for assignment development.
All sessions will be recorded and made available on Blackboard.
Library Session (optional)
To assist students with performing Critical Appraisal Assignments, an optional library session on Endnote and database searching have been organised. Students who are unfamiliar with database searching and/or referencing packages, or those who would like to refresh their knowledge, are encouraged attend this session.
Self-paced learning - Modules 1-5: Evaluation of Scientific Literature
These self-paced learning materials are delivered via an interactive, learner-centred approach. Students are required to engage with the content, complete the assigned readings, and critically appraise practice journal articles for each module. As a guide, this will require up to approximately 3 hours of self-directed learning per week.
course_aims: The aim of this course is for you to become a competent user of research evidence, enabling you to critically evaluate scientific literature and support evidence-based practice in health and rehabilitation sciences. This course is designed to enhance your ability to (a) apply research principles and methods to critically evaluate scientific literature to inform better clinical practice, (b) evaluate the effectiveness of intervention options and determine relevant clinical recommendations, (c) appreciate cultural context, First Nation’s research perspectives, and ethical and practical implications of conducting research in clinical settings, and (d) demonstrate effective communication skills to deliver clear and coherent presentation of clinical knowledge and evidence to diverse audiences.

learning_outcomes.description: Apply research principles and methods to understand scientific literature in clinical practice and health-related professions.
Evaluate analytical techniques used in quantitative and qualitative research in clinical settings.
Discuss ethical standards, appreciate cultural competence, and acknowledge Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives in the research context.
Apply research principles and methods to evaluate the effectiveness of intervention options to address clinical challenges.
Demonstrate cognitive skills to review, analyse and synthesise published research to identify and provide solutions to complex clinical problems.
Critically evaluate literature and generate clinical recommendations for complex clinical problems.
Demonstrate effective communication skills to present a clear and coherent exposition of knowledge and ideas to health-related professionals.

assessment_details.title: Assignment 1 - Critical Appraisal of Quantitative Literature - Individual Written (Modules 1-4)
assessment_details.task_description: This assignment aims to develop students’ ability to find, read, and critically analyse verifiable literature on a clinically relevant topic, with emphasis on systematic reviews and intervention studies. Students will critically evaluate the evidence by examining strengths, limitations, and clinical applicability, and synthesise findings to inform practice. Using a provided clinical scenario and question, students will analyse a given systematic review and identify three additional intervention studies. Students will integrate and evaluate the evidence to generate justified, evidence-based recommendations to guide colleagues within your discipline. The assignment ends with a concise critical appraisal report that outlines a recommended therapy while acknowledging potential limitations and contextual challenges in applying the evidence. Students will receive a relevant systematic review and are required to identify three additional relevant intervention studies. Maximum word limit of 2200 words (excluding title/reference pages) Your assignment should include a maximum of 10 references in total : the provided systematic review, three relevant intervention studies selected by you, and up to six additional supporting references. Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Please see the Assignment Task Sheet [ A1 ] for details. assessment_details.title: Assignment 2 - Critical Appraisal of Qualitative Literature - Group Presentation (Video) (Module 5)
assessment_details.other_conditions: Time limited, Secure. See the conditions definitions
assessment_details.task_description: This assessment is designed to develop students’ ability to critically engage with qualitative research and apply it meaningfully within a clinical context. Through a recorded journal club presentation, students will demonstrate their capacity to analyse qualitative research, evaluate the trustworthiness and relevance of findings, and interpret their implications for practice. They will also consider ethical, cultural, and/or Aboriginal and Torres Strait Islander perspectives, while communicating their insights clearly and professionally to a defined target audience. Working collaboratively, students will analyse complex information and apply evidence to inform clinical reasoning and decision-making within a real-world context . In groups of four , students will create an 8–10 mins recorded journal club presentation based on a provided qualitative research article. Maximum length of the group presentation is 10 mins - Marker will stop watching after 10 mins so any content over this limit will not count towards your mark for the assessment task. Your presentation should include the assigned qualitative article, along with up to 4 additional sources to support your presentation (a maximum of 5 references in total ) While a group mark is typically awarded for the group video presentation, individual marks may be adjusted to reflect each student’s demonstrated contribution, including participation in the recorded presentation. When a student is required to complete an oral or practical assessment item worth 20% or more, the performance will be recorded and retained per Appendix 1. (Assessment Procedure (95)). Artificial Intelligence (AI) and Machine Translation (MT) are emerging tools that may support students in completing this assessment task. Students may appropriately use AI and/or MT in completing this assessment task. Students must clearly reference any use of AI or MT in each instance. A failure to reference generative AI or MT use may constitute student misconduct under the Student Code of Conduct. Please see the Assignment Task Sheet [ A2 ] for details. assessment_details.task_description: Six short quizzes will be conducted during scheduled tutorial sessions across the semester. These are designed to assess your overall understanding of key concepts in quantitative and qualitative methods, including systematic reviews, covered across the modules. Each quiz will consist of multiple-choice questions and will be completed under closed-book conditions. Quizzes must be completed in person during tutorials, and any missed quiz will receive a mark of zero. To provide some flexibility, your final quiz grade will be calculated based on your best four results out of the six quizzes. This assessment task is to be completed in-person during tutorials.
